ideas.title: Sail it yourself, live: the 3D sail box rides with the cart
ideas.goal: Jump in on the land yacht and sail the beach: pull the sheet in and out, steer with the tiller, feel it surge when the trim is right and bog when you over-sheet and the sail stalls. Fun because the right trim changes with every heading and gust, and you find it by feel.
ideas.toward: The cart moves for the first time, on its own wind; the dynamo on its axle (next step) needs a turning wheel. The 3D box is the only flow that stalls the right way (s165/s166: trimmed L/D 3.3, stalled 0.8).
ideas.idea: The 3D WaterLily box hugging the sail steps on the GPU beside the frame (~400k cells, ~real time), re-aimed at the apparent wind every step; its pressure force drives the cart on wheelsand rolling resistance. The sail swings on its sheet (the boom angle is the player's), the cart's speed changes the apparent wind, which changes the flow. Watching: the yacht slides off along the waterline, sail filling, then slows when it is pinned in too hard.
ideas.form: Mini game 'Sail the beach' in the landyacht plugin (keys for sheet and tiller), published; a traced chase-camera film of a played run.

ideas.title: Tack up the beach: the friends cross the deck at every turn
ideas.goal: Reach the far cairn, which lies upwind: you can only get there by zig-zagging, and at each tack you call the friends across so the cart doesn't heel over. Fun because timing the tack, the trim and the crew move is a skill you get better at.
ideas.toward: Friends get a real job on the cart (#754), and their real masses (#745) decide how much sail it can carry: the same masses later ride the electric cart up the dune.
ideas.idea: The solved sail force has a heeling moment about the lee wheels; the friends' masses and where they sit hold it down. Through the tack the sail luffs, the cart slows (from the flow), the friends scramble across with real steps. Too slow a crew move and the windward wheels lift. Watching: four pony-sized friends shuffling across a plank deck while the sail swings over.
ideas.form: Course of driftwood posts on the beach in the yacht mini game; a traced film of one tack.

ideas.title: A lamp on the axle: sail into dusk and your speed is your light
ideas.goal: Sail at dusk with a filament lamp on the mast wired to a dynamo on the wheel: the faster you go, the brighter the beach around you. Fun because a good run is something you SEE, a pool of warm light racing along the dark waterline.
ideas.toward: The dynamo is the motor run backwards (road step): its EMF from the turning coil, the lamp's heat from circuit.jl/hotrod.jl, the first electricity the wind makes.
ideas.idea: motor.jl's drum rotor driven by the axle through a friction roller gives EMF ~ speed; the circuit solver sets the current through a thin wire filament whose temperature (heat balance, radiation) sets its glow; that glow is a real Hikari light that lights the sand, sail and friends. Watching: the lamp flickers orange in a lull, flares white in a gust.
ideas.form: Dynamo + lamp parts on the yacht plugin; a traced dusk film from beside the course.

ideas.title: The sail is cloth: it bellies in its own flow and rips in a gust
ideas.goal: Choose how tight to stretch the canvas and how to patch it; in a gust a weak seam tears and the sail flogs. Fun because you mend and reinforce what broke, and your own patches are what hold next time.
ideas.toward: The yacht's sail stops being a rigid arc; it is also the cloth for the cart's later cover and the windmill's sails.
ideas.idea: A PrintSim membrane (FEM cloth on Mantle) loaded by the box's surface pressure, the box re-measuring the cloth shape each few steps (two-way). Seam strength from stitch count; tearing when the stress passes it. Watching: the sail fills with a real belly, then a seam opens with a crack and the leech flaps wildly.
ideas.form: Physics module + the yacht's sail in the game; a slow-motion traced film of the tear.

ideas.title: Pitch the windmill: four cloth sails turning the dynamo on the dune
ideas.goal: Build a windmill on the dune top, set its blade pitch and how much cloth is out, and keep it from running away in a gust. Fun because the wind is never the same and you tend it like a fire.
ideas.toward: The big goal's charging station: what the windmill makes charges the plates the cart runs on.
ideas.idea: Each blade is the same solved-flow sail at its local apparent wind (blade-element on the 3D box's force curves taken live, not tabled), torque turns the rotor against the dynamo's load from the circuit. Feathering stalls the blades by themselves. Watching: four canvas sails creaking round faster and faster, a friend hauling cloth in as the gust comes.
ideas.form: New windmill plugin on the dune, a traced film at evening wind.

ideas.title: Forming the lead plates: they fizz while they learn to hold charge
ideas.goal: Charge, discharge and recharge your lead plates to 'form' them; each cycle they hold more. Fun because the battery you build is yours, and it gets better the more patiently you work it.
ideas.toward: Planté's accumulator, the cart's fuel tank (road step).
ideas.idea: Electrochemistry on the plates: lead oxidises to PbO2 at the anode, the porous layer grows per cycle (capacity from layer depth), gassing begins when the plate is full and the bubbles' volume is Faraday's law from the current. Watching: in a glass jar on the bench, plates darken brown, then fine bubbles stream up when you've overcharged.
ideas.form: Physics module + jars on the motor bench; a close traced film of the fizz.

ideas.title: A blue spark at the commutator when you break the circuit
ideas.goal: Throw the cart's switch at full speed and see the spark jump; ride it gently and it stays dark. Fun because the spark is the machine telling you how hard you pushed it.
ideas.toward: The 'commutator sparks blue in the dark' moment of the big goal, from real L di/dt, not a particle effect.
ideas.idea: The wound coil's inductance from its geometry (em.jl), the voltage spike when current is cut fast, and a gap breakdown at ~3 kV/mm in air: a spark only when the spike passes it; its brightness is an emissive channel in the tracer. Watching: in the dark workshop, a crackling blue flash at the brushes when the cart stops hard.
ideas.form: Physics in motor.jl/circuit.jl; a traced night still and a 5 s film.

ideas.title: Kite traction: fly a cloth kite from the cart and let it drag you
ideas.goal: Fly a kite on a line from the cart and steer it through the wind window: diving it across the sky pulls hardest. Fun because figure-eights at the right moment yank the cart forward.
ideas.toward: A second way the cart takes the wind, with the same 3D sail flow (a kite is a sail with no mast).
ideas.idea: The kite is the cambered membrane in its own flow box at its apparent wind (wind + its own motion), the line a rope (XPBD) to the cart; steering lines twist its angle. Watching: a patched kite swooping across the evening sky, the cart lurching along the sand behind it.
ideas.form: Mini game on the beach; a traced wide film.

ideas.title: Race yesterday: the island's wind is recorded, and you sail against your own ghost
ideas.goal: Every evening sail the same course in that day's wind and race the ghost of yesterday's run. Fun because the wind decides who wins: a gusty day beats a calm one, and you try to beat your own trim.
ideas.toward: 'Runs on yesterday's wind': the daily rhythm of the big goal, the weather as what you come back for.
ideas.idea: The island's wind (wind.jl) is logged; a run records the cart's path; the ghost replays as a translucent cart. The live box flies today's sail. Watching: two yachts along the waterline, one of them a glassy ghost.
ideas.form: Feature in the yacht mini game; a film of a close finish.

ideas.title: Hike out or go over: the cart lifts two wheels in a gust
ideas.goal: In a gust the windward wheels leave the sand; you ease the sheet or send a friend out on the plank to hold it down. Fun because riding on two wheels is a thrill you can push too far.
ideas.toward: Friends' real masses on the cart; the rigid-body cart on wheels that the electric cart needs.
ideas.idea: The cart is a rigid body (PrintSim) with four wheel contacts on sand; the solved sail force's heeling moment against the crew's weight and position; past the tipping point it falls over by itself, the sail lands on the sand. Watching: a cart skimming on two wheels with a friend hanging off the windward edge.
ideas.form: Rigid-body cart in the yacht plugin; traced film.
